semantics.purpose: Plan security-audit investigation surfaces without treating checklist completion as proof of safety.
semantics.coverageUnit: subsystem × trust boundary × applicable attack class
semantics.zeroFindingsRule: Zero findings never proves that an attack class is covered.
semantics.applicabilityRule: Plan only attack classes supported by reconnaissance evidence; non-applicable classes must be explained rather than silently omitted.

evidenceContract.rule: A candidate without a concrete boundary failure or security outcome remains an unresolved hypothesis or open question.

classes.title: Injection and unsafe interpretation
classes.question: Can attacker-controlled input cross a parser, interpreter, query, template, shell, or serialization boundary with insufficient control?
appliesWhen: untrusted input reaches SQL, NoSQL, shell, template, HTML, expression, path, or deserialization sinks
dynamic query, command, template, or code construction exists
investigate: trace source-to-sink data flow
identify encoding, validation, parameterization, escaping, or allowlist controls
verify the control is applied on every relevant path
notSufficient: presence of validation somewhere in the subsystem
absence of an obvious exploit string

classes.title: Authentication and authorization
classes.question: Can a principal authenticate as another identity, exceed its granted authority, or invoke a privileged operation without the intended authorization decision?
appliesWhen: authentication, session, token, role, permission, policy, or privileged-operation code exists
identity or authorization claims cross service boundaries
investigate: trace identity establishment and propagation
identify authorization decision points and default-deny behavior
verify object- and action-level checks at the enforcement boundary
notSufficient: authentication success alone
UI-level hiding of privileged actions

classes.title: Tenant and account isolation
classes.question: Can one tenant, account, workspace, or organization read or mutate another tenant's resources through identifier, query, cache, storage, or policy confusion?
appliesWhen: multi-tenant, organization, workspace, account, or namespace concepts exist
tenant-scoped identifiers or shared storage are used
investigate: trace tenant context from entry point to storage and cache keys
verify tenant ownership is enforced independently of caller-supplied identifiers
inspect background jobs and cross-service calls for lost tenant context
notSufficient: tenant id existing in the request
database rows containing a tenant column without enforced scoping

classes.title: Sensitive data lifecycle
classes.question: Can sensitive data be exposed, retained, logged, replicated, exported, or deleted inconsistently with its intended protection and lifecycle?
appliesWhen: personal, credential, financial, confidential, regulated, or otherwise sensitive data is stored or transmitted
retention, deletion, export, backup, logging, encryption, or residency behavior exists
investigate: map collection, storage, transit, logs, backups, exports, and deletion paths
identify encryption and access controls at each boundary
verify deletion and retention semantics include derived and replicated data where relevant
notSufficient: encryption at one layer
a documented retention policy without matching source behavior

classes.title: Software supply chain
classes.question: Can untrusted dependency, artifact, build input, package lifecycle behavior, or provenance gap alter trusted output or execution?
appliesWhen: third-party dependencies, plugins, actions, containers, generated artifacts, or package lifecycle hooks exist
build or release inputs cross external trust boundaries
investigate: identify externally controlled build and dependency inputs
inspect pinning, integrity, provenance, and update boundaries
trace whether install or build hooks can execute with privileged credentials
notSufficient: dependency version freshness alone
lockfile presence without integrity or provenance analysis

classes.title: Cloud and deployment boundary
classes.question: Can deployment configuration, IAM, secret distribution, network exposure, or environment separation grant unintended access or execution capability?
appliesWhen: cloud infrastructure, containers, deployment manifests, IAM, secrets, CI/CD, or environment configuration exists
production or shared infrastructure boundaries are represented in source
investigate: trace identities and privileges used by build, deploy, and runtime components
inspect public exposure and network trust assumptions
verify secret and environment boundaries do not collapse across stages
notSufficient: private repository status
cloud-provider defaults assumed to be secure without source evidence

classes.title: RPC and messaging trust boundaries
classes.question: Can messages, events, jobs, webhooks, or RPC calls cross a trust boundary without authenticated origin, authorization, integrity, replay, ordering, or schema controls required by the operation?
appliesWhen: queues, events, jobs, RPC, webhooks, callbacks, or service-to-service messages exist
asynchronous or remote actions can mutate state
investigate: identify sender and receiver principals
trace message authentication, authorization, integrity, freshness, and idempotency controls
verify privileged effects are re-authorized at the consumer boundary
notSufficient: network location alone as sender identity
schema validation alone for privileged messages

classes.title: Resource exhaustion and abuse
classes.question: Can an untrusted principal force disproportionate CPU, memory, storage, process, queue, network, token, or external-service consumption across a shared boundary?
appliesWhen: user-controlled work can fan out, recurse, allocate, enqueue, upload, query, or invoke paid/external resources
shared quotas or multi-tenant capacity exist
investigate: trace attacker-controlled amplification factors
identify quotas, bounds, timeouts, cancellation, and backpressure at the controlling boundary
check whether one principal can consume resources assigned to others
notSufficient: average-case performance
a timeout that does not bound upstream or queued work

classes.title: Browser and client trust boundary
classes.question: Can browser, mobile, desktop, extension, or other client-controlled state be trusted as an authorization, integrity, confidentiality, or origin guarantee?
appliesWhen: browser or client code handles security-sensitive state, tokens, redirects, messaging, storage, or privileged requests
server decisions depend on client-supplied claims or UI state
investigate: separate client convenience checks from server enforcement
inspect origin, redirect, storage, token, cross-window, and cross-site boundaries
trace whether client-modifiable state can authorize server-side effects
notSufficient: disabled or hidden UI controls
client-side validation as an authorization boundary

classes.title: AI and agent security
classes.question: Can untrusted model input, retrieved content, tool output, memory, or delegated instruction cross into privileged tool use, secret access, data mutation, or policy bypass?
appliesWhen: LLMs, agents, tool calling, retrieval, prompt assembly, memory, MCP/plugins, or autonomous actions exist
model-controlled output can influence privileged operations
investigate: map instruction and data trust boundaries separately
trace model-controlled values into tools, credentials, files, network, and state mutation
verify capability scoping, confirmation, provenance, and output validation at tool boundaries
notSufficient: system-prompt wording alone as a security boundary
model refusal behavior without deterministic capability controls
